title: CPU Performance
intro: A short, independent catch-up: learn the essential knowledge, practise and review answers.

questions.prompt: For cost = price × quantity, which is an input?
Which CPU characteristic helps run several independent tasks concurrently?
questions.feedback: Extra cores may support parallel workloads.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the explanations, visual and model before answering.

blocks.title: Clock speed
blocks.text: Clock speed is measured in hertz (Hz). A higher clock speed means the CPU carries out more clock cycles each second, so it can generally process instructions faster.

blocks.title: Cache size
blocks.text: Cache is small, fast memory used to store frequently used data and instructions. A larger cache can reduce the need to fetch them from slower main memory (RAM), improving performance.

blocks.title: Number of cores
blocks.text: A core processes instructions. A processor with more cores can process more tasks at the same time, which can improve performance when several programs are running.

blocks.title: Compare before you decide
blocks.text: Look at all three factors: clock speed, cache size and number of cores. For example, one CPU may have a higher clock speed while another has more cores and a larger cache. Explain which factors matter for the stated task.

blocks.title: Visual model
blocks.caption: Use these linked concepts to explain your answer.

blocks.title: Worked example · Using the CPU A and CPU B specifications shown, explain TWO reasons CPU B may be better for running several programs at the same time. [4 marks]
blocks.text: Read the specifications shown: CPU A has the higher clock speed. CPU B has more cores and a larger cache. The task involves running several programs. First reason: CPU B has four cores rather than two [1]. More cores can process more tasks at the same time, improving multitasking [1]. Second reason: CPU B has 8 MB cache rather than 4 MB [1]. More frequently used data and instructions can be accessed quickly, reducing slower RAM access [1]. Check the command word 'explain': each reason must link a CPU characteristic to an improvement. CPU A's higher clock speed is a valid comparison, but we cannot guarantee which CPU is faster in every task.

items: Clock speed — The number of clock cycles the CPU carries out per second, measured in hertz.
Hertz (Hz) — Unit of clock speed: one clock cycle per second.
Cache — Small, fast memory that stores frequently used data and instructions for the CPU.
CPU core — Part of a CPU that processes instructions.
Parallel processing — Processing more than one task at the same time using multiple CPU cores.

blocks.text:
A college chooses a CPU for computers running several applications.
CPU G: 3.9 GHz, 2 cores, 6 MB cache.
CPU H: 3.1 GHz, 8 cores, 16 MB cache.
Explain TWO reasons why CPU H could be better for this use. [4 marks]

questions.prompt: The code compares clockJ = 2.6 with clockK = 3.4. What is printed?
options: CPU K has an equal or higher clock speed
CPU J has a higher clock speed
questions.answer: CPU K has an equal or higher clock speed

questions.prompt: If clockJ becomes 3.8, which result is printed?
options: CPU J has a higher clock speed
CPU K has an equal or higher clock speed
questions.answer: CPU J has a higher clock speed

questions.prompt: For multitasking, why might 6 cores be preferable to 2?
options: More tasks can run in parallel
Six cores guarantee triple clock speed
More cores permanently save more files
More cores prevent all RAM access
questions.answer: More tasks can run in parallel
questions.feedback: Additional cores may process concurrent work.

writing.prompt:
A college chooses a CPU for computers running several applications.
CPU G: 3.9 GHz, 2 cores, 6 MB cache.
CPU H: 3.1 GHz, 8 cores, 16 MB cache.
Explain TWO reasons why CPU H could be better for this use. [4 marks]
writing.model: CPU H has eight cores rather than two [1], so it can process more tasks at the same time [1]. CPU H has 16 MB cache rather than 6 MB [1], so more frequently used instructions/data can be accessed quickly, reducing slower RAM accesses [1]. CPU G has the higher clock speed; the best choice depends on the workload. Original practice marking points, not an official OCR mark scheme.
